content.user_title: Plan Agile Tasks and User Stories
content.value_statement: Teams often receive broad feature requests without clear tasks, priorities, or acceptance criteria. This skill turns feature ideas into user stories, sprint backlog items, dependencies, and Definition of Done checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates INVEST-style user stories with acceptance criteria.
Breaks epics into stories and implementation tasks.
Applies MoSCoW prioritization to backlog items.
Builds sprint plans with goals, capacity, velocity, and selected stories.
Defines task board columns and Definition of Done checks.
limitations: Does not connect to issue trackers or update tickets automatically.
Does not estimate actual team capacity without user-provided data.
Does not replace product owner decisions on scope or priority.
Uses generic Agile examples that should be adapted to local process.

use_cases.title: Convert Features Into Backlog Items
use_cases.description: Turn a product idea into user stories, acceptance criteria, technical notes, dependencies, and priority labels.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sprint Planning
use_cases.description: Select sprint work based on goal, capacity, velocity, dependencies, and Definition of Done requirements.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Growing Backlog
use_cases.description: Group related work, split large stories, remove vague requirements, and organize items by priority.

prompt_templates.title: Create a User Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this feature into an INVEST user story with acceptance criteria, technical notes, dependencies, and priority: [feature].

prompt_templates.title: Break Down an Epic
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a larger initiative.
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this epic into user stories and implementation tasks. Include story points, dependencies, and test tasks: [epic].

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize these backlog items with MoSCoW labels. Explain the reason for each priority and identify items to split: [items].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sprint Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with capacity and delivery constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sprint plan using this goal, team capacity, velocity, dependencies, and backlog. Include selected stories and Definition of Done: [details].

output_examples.input: Feature: Let users reset passwords by email.
output_examples.output: A password reset user story with acceptance criteria for valid email, expired links, weak passwords, and confirmation messaging.

output_examples.input: Epic: Build user account management for a web app.
output_examples.output: An epic breakdown with registration, login, profile, password reset, security tasks, estimates, and dependencies.

output_examples.input: Backlog: registration, login, profile images, social login, account deletion.
output_examples.output: A MoSCoW priority list that separates required authentication work from optional account enhancements.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, target users, and constraints before asking for a plan.
Include team capacity, velocity, and deadlines for sprint planning prompts.
Review generated acceptance criteria with engineering, QA, and product stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Asking for estimates without scope, team size, or delivery constraints.
Treating generated priorities as final business decisions.
Keeping stories at epic size instead of splitting high-point items.

faq.question: Can this skill write Jira tickets?
faq.answer: It can draft ticket-ready text, but it does not connect to Jira or create tickets.

faq.question: Does it support Scrum and Kanban?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes sprint planning guidance and a basic task board structure.

faq.question: Can it estimate story points?
faq.answer: It can suggest relative estimates when scope and complexity are provided.

faq.question: Will it replace sprint planning meetings?
faq.answer: No. It prepares structured planning material for team review and decision-making.

faq.question: Does it need access to source code?
faq.answer: No. Architecture details can improve the technical tasks, but source code is not required.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: This report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
